clinicalPearls: Neonatal skeletal dysplasia within the type XI collagenopathy spectrum, presenting with rhizomelic (proximal) limb shortening, a flat midface, a small upturned nose and micrognathia.
Sensorineural hearing loss is a defining feature, reflecting the structural role of type XI collagen in the inner ear.
Cleft palate and Pierre Robin sequence (micrognathia, glossoptosis and neonatal airway compromise) are frequent and drive early management.
Infantile radiographs show dumbbell-shaped femora and humeri from metaphyseal broadening, and these tend to remodel with growth.
A key distinguishing feature is catch-up limb growth — the rhizomelia and dumbbell long bones improve with age, unlike most severe fixed neonatal dysplasias.
Associated with COL11A2 variants and allelic with otospondylomegaepiphyseal dysplasia (OSMED) and non-ocular (type III) Stickler syndrome, with which it overlaps clinically.
Because COL11A2, unlike COL2A1 and COL11A1, is not expressed in the eye, the ocular and retinal complications of classic Stickler syndrome are characteristically absent — a useful separator.
Hearing loss and airway/feeding issues, rather than the skeletal changes, dominate the long-term burden.
reference.pathophysiology: Weissenbacher-Zweymuller syndrome belongs to the type XI collagenopathies and is associated with variants in COL11A2, which encodes the alpha-2 chain of type XI collagen. Type XI collagen co-assembles with type II collagen to regulate the diameter and spacing of cartilage collagen fibrils and is also a structural component of the inner ear, so its deficiency produces both a chondrodysplasia (rhizomelic shortening with dumbbell-shaped long bones, midface hypoplasia and cleft palate) and sensorineural hearing loss. Because COL11A2, unlike COL2A1 and COL11A1, is not expressed in the vitreous of the eye, the ocular and retinal complications of classic Stickler syndrome are characteristically absent. The condition is allelic with, and lies on a clinical spectrum including, otospondylomegaepiphyseal dysplasia (OSMED) and non-ocular (type III) Stickler syndrome, and the neonatal skeletal changes characteristically remodel with growth rather than remaining fixed.
additionalDifferentials: Otospondylomegaepiphyseal dysplasia (OSMED), the allelic recessive disorder
Stickler syndrome types I to III
additionalInvestigations: Skeletal survey in infancy with serial follow-up films to document long-bone remodelling
Molecular testing of COL11A2 or a collagenopathy gene panel
Cleft palate, airway and feeding assessment
Ophthalmology review to exclude Stickler-type eye disease
Sleep study where obstructive breathing is suspected
Genetic counselling clarifying the inheritance pattern in the family
redFlags: Neonatal airway obstruction from Pierre Robin sequence
Progressive or undetected sensorineural hearing loss affecting speech development
reference.prognosis: Growth outlook is generally favourable, with limb proportions and long-bone shape improving over childhood; sensorineural hearing loss persists and requires long-term audiological support.
pitfalls: Mistaking it for a lethal or fixed severe dysplasia and missing the expected catch-up growth
Overlooking sensorineural hearing loss in infancy
Searching for retinal disease that COL11A2 does not cause
Misassigning inheritance (dominant versus recessive) and giving inaccurate recurrence counselling
references: International nosology and classification of genetic skeletal disorders
Standard clinical genetics and dysmorphology reference texts
management: Prioritise neonatal airway management for Pierre Robin sequence, using prone positioning and a nasopharyngeal airway and escalating to surgical measures if obstruction is severe
Support feeding with cleft-palate feeding techniques and specialist input, and undertake surgical cleft palate repair at the appropriate age
Provide long-term audiological support with hearing aids for the persistent sensorineural hearing loss
Monitor the skeleton with serial radiographs, anticipating favourable remodelling of the dumbbell long bones and catch-up limb growth over childhood
Arrange ophthalmology review to exclude Stickler-type eye disease, which is characteristically absent in this collagenopathy
Confirm the diagnosis by COL11A2 testing and offer genetic counselling regarding inheritance and recurrence risk
Coordinate care through a multidisciplinary team including cleft, ENT and audiology, respiratory and genetics services
